root_cause.statement: Postgres trigger lock on bd_ma_stylecolorchannelattributes. The older md_trigger_on_update (and exit_trigger_on_update) WHEN clause includes old.erlstmkdnwk < old.plan_current (old.exitdate < old.plan_current). When it's true, md_trigger_on_update_validity_check() sets erlstmkdnwk = OLD.erlstmkdnwk in the same save transaction. For an item already in markdown, a relaunch's new MD Wk is therefore silently undone, while Relaunch and Exit keep their new values. Replan and both screens then show the reverted Postgres value. QA removed the clause directly in the DB. The trigger DDL isn't in any repo or release process, so environments drifted. Bonus (live Staging) already has QA's version today, and the retest passes.

knowledge_gained.technical: Boden lifecycle rules live in Postgres triggers on bd_ma_stylecolorchannelattributes, and none are in git. AFTER UPDATE OF <col> triggers with WHEN guards call *_validity_check() functions that reset the column to OLD inside the save transaction, with no error back to the UI; pg_trigger_depth()=0 prevents recursion. The UI reads lifecycle weeks (Style Edit REST + Floorset attribute: columns) and its current week/range (bd_serviceparams) from Postgres. ClickHouse bd_ma_stylecolorchannelattributes is append-only history, and item lists come from ClickHouse pivots. So 'reverts after replan' usually means the PG row was already reverted at save. Environments drift silently because trigger DDL has no repo, so identify the app's live DB (bd_serviceparams + max(updated_at) vs the UI week) before trusting a dump.
knowledge_gained.functional: Once an item is in markdown (MD Wk before the current plan week), its MD week is history and is normally locked: the UI picker greys out passed weeks, and the old DB trigger enforced the same lock. A relaunch starts a new lifecycle, so a new future MD week is legitimate even though the old one has passed; the old lock didn't account for relaunch. QA's fix removes the lock entirely, so MD/Exit can now be moved for any in-MD item, not only relaunched ones. That's a product decision to confirm before promoting to Prod.
